The displacement (in meters) of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=4{t}^{3}-{t}^{2},$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the time when the particle's acceleration is equal to $a=70\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

The acceleration is $70\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ at
$t=$
{{field-1}} seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}) \\  & =12{t}^{2}-2t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12{t}^{2}-2t) \\  & =24t-2\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the time when the acceleration is $a=70,$ we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}70 & =24t-2 \\ 24t & =72 \\ t & =3\text{ }\text{s}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the acceleration is $70\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ at $t=3$ seconds.
